points.note: Lower ball-chain sprocket on the green crank-axle post at the base. This is the SECOND sprocket (down at the crank axle), NOT the required upper pinion. Added per spec allowance. The required pinion is occluded (see occluded list).
Left brass helical cylinder gear seen roughly end-on; dot = center of the circular (obliquely-foreshortened) end face. Clearest of the two cylinder gears.

Center brass geared cylinder (large brass gear wheel + helical body) seen end-on; dot = hub/axle bolt = projected rotation axis. Larger/more prominent, but partly occluded by a black bracket arch. CAVEAT: this could alternatively be the LARGE brass crank drive gear rather than a cylinder gear (the pinion would sit coaxially in front of it, hidden from the rear).

Topmost/frontmost rocker arm of the fan. The ~20 arms overlap into a dense bundle; the free chamfered TIP ends fan out at the image-left. This dot = lower width-corner of the top arm's tip. The arm runs horizontally left->right, so the two tip corners differ mainly in height (upper/lower); 'left/right' here denote the two width edges.
Same top arm; upper/outer width-corner of the chamfered tip. Individual arms are hard to separate in this broadside fan, hence low confidence.
Upper-left outer corner of the green top-frame casting (image-left end, near/back face).

occluded.reason: Rear view: the upper chain sprocket / pinion (next to the large brass crank drive gear) is hidden behind the fan of rocker arms and the drive gear itself. The ball chain is visible running up and disappearing behind the rocker-arm bundle.

No brass cone gear is separately resolvable from behind. The one prominent cone-shaped part is the green-painted STEEL cone_pivot_post (repo part cone-pivot-post, MHA-016), not the brass cone_gear (MHA-013); the brass cone gear, if present, is buried among the occluded/overlapping base brass cluster.
The wide butt/pivot ends of the rocker arms are at the image-right, hidden behind the right frame leg / drive column.
Same: butt ends occluded behind the right frame leg.

orientation_note: BACK view: the camera faces the rear of the machine (crank hidden on the far/front side). Corner left/right are AS SEEN IN THE IMAGE (image-left = _left). The near vertical face is the machine's back, so every visible outer corner is labeled 'back_*'; the matching 'front_*' corners are on the far side and occluded. Because this is a rear view, image-left corresponds to the machine's own right-hand side.
